title: Lesson Plan — The Raven and the Fox (Class 6 CBSE English)
subject: English
objectives: Identify the characters and main events of the fable.
Use key vocabulary (flatter, vain, pride, cunning, sense) correctly.
Explain how the fox tricks the raven.
State the moral and apply it to real-life situations.
Identify pronouns, direct speech, adverbs, and rhyming pairs.
prerequisites: Familiarity with story-reading and fables (Chapter 1: A Bottle of Dew).
Basic recognition of nouns, verbs, adjectives.
materials: Photocopies of the fable (poem + prose) — one per student
Cards with vocabulary words and meanings for matching
Handout listing pairs of rhyming and non-rhyming words
Worksheet — The Raven and the Fox

activities.description: Hook with a real-life question: 'Have you ever noticed someone praising another person a lot, and then asking them for a favour?' Take 2-3 examples from students.
student_actions: Predict what the fable might be about.

activities.description: Read the fable aloud — first the poem, then the prose retelling. Students follow along on their handouts.
teacher_actions: Ask 'what will the fox do next?' once.

activities.description: Cover four blocks: (i) characters and plot; (ii) vocabulary game; (iii) pronouns + direct speech with examples from the fable; (iv) adverbs (-ly) and rhyming pairs.
teacher_actions: Map the trick step-by-step on the board.
List rhyming pairs from the poem.

activities.description: Worksheet: 5 questions covering comprehension, vocabulary, pronouns, direct speech, and the moral.
Set homework — write a short fable with a moral, in the spirit of Aesop. Preview the next chapter.

homework: Write your own short fable (5-7 sentences) with a clear moral.
Find 5 pairs of rhyming words from the poem and write each pair.
Convert this sentence to direct speech: The fox told the raven that he had a beautiful voice.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 10-question chapter quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on writing-your-own-fable using a creativity + grammar rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading on the homework fable using a moral-clarity rubric.
references: NCERT Class 6 English Poorvi, Unit 1: Fables and Folk Tales — The Raven and the Fox.
